heroIntro: Under Sections 39 and 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, any landowner whose title is clouded by a forged deed, fraudulent Power of Attorney, or wrong khatian record can file a civil suit for declaration of title and cancellation of the voidable instrument. Under Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908, deed cancellation suits must generally be filed within 3 years of discovering the fraud.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Declaratory & Deed Cancellation Suits
points: Governing Laws: Specific Relief Act, 1877 (Sections 39 & 42), Limitation Act, 1908 (Articles 91 & 120), Court-Fees Act, 1870.
Limitation Window: 3 years from knowledge of the forged deed (Article 91); 6 years for pure declaration (Article 120).
Court Fee: Fixed fee for pure declaration; ad valorem fee under Section 7(iv)(c) when consequential relief (cancellation/possession) is sought.
Jurisdiction: Assistant Judge or Joint District Judge Court depending on the pecuniary valuation of the suit property.

sections.h2: When to File a Declaratory Suit vs Deed Cancellation Suit
sections.content:
Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 empowers any person entitled to a legal character or right to property to sue any person denying that right for a court declaration of their title. However, the proviso to Section 42 bars a pure declaratory suit if the plaintiff is able to seek further relief—such as recovery of possession or deed cancellation—and omits to do so.

Where a forged sale deed, fraudulent gift deed (Heba), or unauthorised Power of Attorney exists against your property, you must combine a prayer under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 asking the court to adjudge the instrument void or voidable and order it delivered up and cancelled. Upon passing a decree under Section 39, the court sends a copy to the Sub-Registrar under Section 39(2) to endorse the cancellation in the official register.

If your primary issue is an erroneous BS or RS Khatian without a forged deed, consult a land lawyer in Bangladesh or review our guide on checking land ownership and mutation records.

Strict limitation periods under the Limitation Act, 1908 determine whether your suit is maintainable, making prompt filing upon discovery essential for both resident and NRB owners.

Because NRBs often discover forged deeds years after registration, proving the exact date of knowledge—such as through a certified search receipt or travel passport entry—is critical under Article 91. You can also pursue parallel criminal prosecution for forgery under Sections 467 and 468 of the Penal Code; see our land recovery guide and criminal defence & prosecution services.

sections.h2: Court Fees and Pecuniary Jurisdiction in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 and the Civil Courts Act, 1887 (as amended), the valuation of your suit determines both the court fee payable and which civil court hears the case. A pure declaratory suit under Section 42 without consequential relief carries a nominal fixed court fee (Schedule II, Article 17(iii)).

However, when you seek cancellation of a deed under Section 39 or recovery of possession alongside a declaration, Section 7(iv)(c) of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 requires paying an ad valorem court fee based on the market value stated in the impugned deed or the property's valuation, subject to statutory caps. Under the amended Civil Courts Act, Assistant Judges hear suits valued up to BDT 15 lakh, Senior Assistant Judges up to BDT 25 lakh, and Joint District Judges above BDT 25 lakh.

Always verify the latest court fee stamp calculation with Advocate Md. Shah Alam before filing, as undervaluation can lead to plaint rejection under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Procedure to Cancel a Forged Deed
sections.content:
Follow this structured civil litigation roadmap to freeze further transfers and cancel a fraudulent instrument:

  1. Conduct Sub-Registry Search & Certified Copy: Obtain a certified copy (Nakal) of the disputed deed and index search certificate from the local Sub-Registry Office.
  2. Apply for Temporary Injunction (Order 39 Rules 1 & 2, CPC 1908): File an injunction petition alongside the plaint to restrain the defendant from selling, mortgaging, or mutating the land during trial.
  3. Request Expert Handwriting/Thumbprint Verification: Move the court under Section 45 of the Evidence Act, 1872 to send the Sub-Registry thumbprint book (Balam/Thumb Impression Register) to the CID Forensic Lab.
  4. Trial & Witness Examination: Examine the Sub-Registrar's clerk, deed writer, and attesting witnesses to establish impersonation or lack of consideration.
  5. Register Decree at Sub-Registry & AC Land: Once decreed under Section 39, transmit the certified decree to the Sub-Registrar for cancellation endorsement and apply for mutation correction at the AC (Land) office.

If the disputed property was already mortgaged to a bank using the forged deed, check our guide on staying bank auctions in Artha Rin Adalat and NRB property due diligence.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for Title & Cancellation Suits
sections.content:
Assemble these certified documents before drafting your plaint under Order 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908:

  • Original title deed (Saf Kabala/Heba/Partition) proving the plaintiff's valid ownership chain.
  • Certified copy of the impugned forged or voidable deed from the Sub-Registry Office.
  • CS, SA, RS, and BS/City Jarip Khatian copies plus Mutation Khatian and Khajna receipts.
  • Passport travel history, visa stamps, or airline records (essential if the NRB owner was abroad on the alleged execution date).
  • Sub-Registry index search report and, for overseas plaintiffs, an Embassy-attested Power of Attorney.

faqs.question: Can I file a declaratory suit if I am not in physical possession of the land?
faqs.answer: Under the proviso to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, you cannot file a suit for mere declaration if you are out of possession. You must include a consequential prayer for recovery of possession under Section 8 and pay the appropriate ad valorem court fee.

faqs.question: What happens if the 3-year limit under Article 91 has already passed?
faqs.answer: For voidable deeds, Article 91 bars cancellation after 3 years from discovery. However, if a deed is void ab initio—such as one executed by a complete impersonator when the owner was abroad—courts may treat it as non-est and entertain a 12-year possession/title suit.

faqs.question: How long does a deed cancellation suit take in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A contested civil suit for declaration and deed cancellation typically takes 2 to 5 years in the trial court, depending on witness availability and forensic examination. Securing a temporary injunction early prevents the defendant from transferring the land meanwhile.

faqs.question: Does the court automatically notify the Sub-Registrar after cancelling a deed?
faqs.answer: Under Section 39(2) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, if the instrument is registered under the Registration Act, 1908, the court sends a copy of its decree to the registering officer, who must note the cancellation on the copy of the instrument in the register.

faqs.question: Can I file both a civil cancellation suit and a criminal forgery case together?
faqs.answer: Yes. Civil suits under Sections 39 and 42 cancel the deed and protect title, while a criminal case under Sections 420, 467, 468, and 471 of the Penal Code prosecutes the forger. Both proceedings can run concurrently without barring each other.
